documented_boundaries: A frame scope is checked against its storage and its nearest enclosing scope only; accesses inside the frame are not restricted to it. Documented in the README; pinned by a positive test.
An exception raised by a pinned semantics module after it starts executing is not rewritten into the error envelope.
probes: boolean in place of an integer in COMPARE result, READ value, location index, result.final, result.best and problem: rejected (SCHEMA_INVALID or PROFILE_SCHEMA_INVALID)
CRLF line ends: NONCANONICAL_LINE; UTF-8 BOM: FRAMING_INVALID; negative index: SCHEMA_INVALID; seed set: PROFILE_INPUT_INVALID
integer outside the RFC 8785 domain: NONCANONICAL_LINE

method: Each raise statement under src/algorithm_trace_core was replaced by pass, one at a time, in a scratch copy, and the library suite was run with -x. Each surviving mutant was then run against the core-isolating controls (tests/core_cases.py), which were first confirmed on the unmutated package: every hostile control is rejected with its code and every positive twin is accepted. Classification follows the observed outcome.

rejection_obligations.definition: An obligation is a distinct (raise site, stable code) pair in canonical, framing, profiles and replay that a hostile control reaches.
shared_obligation_notes: framing.py:43 and replay.py:214 are each reached by a 0.1.0 control and its core-isolating twin. In the unmutated package both hit the same branch. With that branch removed, the 0.1.0 control is still rejected through a backup path (the strict-JSON parse; the example profile's check_argument hook), while the twin is accepted. Only the twin isolates the obligation. These are the only two alias pairs, and both are deliberate.
framing.py:51 re-raises three different strict-JSON failures: a duplicate key and a non-finite number, both detected in canonical.py, and malformed JSON. They are three obligations at one site.
profiles.py:131 is the shared validate_part helper for the problem, precondition and result schemas. They are three obligations at one site.
